root_cause.hypothesis: The write pointer is advanced on the raw request (if (wr_en)) instead of on the accepted write (if (wr_fire)). When the FIFO is full and a write is requested (overflow), the write must be dropped and wr_ptr held; instead wr_ptr increments from 0000 to 0001 at the 325000 edge while rd_ptr stays at 1000, so count = wr_ptr - rd_ptr becomes 9 and full (wrap bits differ AND low bits equal) deasserts. Because full is now 0, wr_fire becomes 1 and the next 'dropped' writes (0xE1, 0xE2) are actually stored into mem, overwriting unread entries (mem[1] changes 00001010 -> 11100001 at 335000), which explains the later rd_data mismatches (got 0xe1 expected 0xa). The pointer is now permanently ahead by the number of dropped writes, so count/empty/full are wrong in every subsequent test.

evidence.interpretation: Pre-edge of first overflow step: FIFO correctly holds 8 entries.
FIFO correctly full before the overflow edge.
Overflow correctly flagged: wr_en while full, so the write must be dropped.
Write is NOT accepted (wr_fire=0) yet, per the RTL, wr_ptr update uses wr_en, not wr_fire.
Write requested during the full cycle.
wr_ptr before the dropped write (wrap bit 0, addr 0) vs rd_ptr 1000 -> full.
wr_ptr advanced despite the write being dropped (wr_fire was 0).
rd_ptr unchanged; no read, so the only state change is the illegal wr_ptr increment.
full deasserted because wr_ptr/rd_ptr low bits no longer match; expected 1.
Second overflow request not flagged because full is wrongly 0.
wr_ptr keeps incrementing every edge with wr_en=1, including the three overflow cycles (325000, 335000, 345000).
rd_ptr stays 1000 (value before window, set at 225000); no reads in this window.
full asserted only for one cycle, then wrongly cleared by the illegal wr_ptr increment.
After the bad increment, wr_fire becomes 1 so the subsequent 'dropped' writes are actually accepted into memory.
count exceeds DEPTH (9, 10, 11), matching sim.log errors.
Unread entry mem[1] (was 00001010 = 0x0a) overwritten with overflow data 0xE1; explains later rd_data got 0xe1 expected 0xa.
Overflow stimulus 0xE0, 0xE1, 0xE2 applied in the three overflow steps.

alternative_hypotheses_considered: full flag equation (line 54-55) wrong: rejected; full was correctly 1 at 321000 with wr_ptr=0000, rd_ptr=1000, and correctly evaluates to 0 for wr_ptr=0001; the error is in the pointer state, not the comparator.
count arithmetic (line 56) wrong: rejected; count = wr_ptr - rd_ptr is consistent with the pointer values in every query (0001-1000 = 1001).
Memory write enable (line 78) wrong: rejected; it correctly uses wr_fire. The memory corruption at 335000 is a secondary effect of full being wrongly 0.
Read-side bug (rd_ptr/rd_fire): rejected; rd_ptr did not move in the failing window and fill/drain tests passed.
Testbench/model error: rejected; spec says writes while full are dropped and must not change state, which the model implements.
limitations: Diagnosis is a hypothesis supported by waveform evidence and RTL reading, not a formal proof; the fix (wr_en -> wr_fire on line 67) was not re-simulated because re-running the simulator was out of scope. Later-test failures were attributed to the persistent pointer offset without exhaustively tracing each one.
